After Nf4, White has Bxf4, winning the knight. Not good. 

So far, **Kxb7** is clearly the best move. It wins material cleanly with a forcing sequence. Let me verify the main line one more time to make sure:

**Main line:**
1. **Kxb7** (Black captures knight)
2. **Bxa7** (White's best try, capturing the a7 pawn)
3. **Kxa7** (Black captures bishop, up material overall)

After this sequence, Black has won a knight and a bishop for one pawn - a decisive material advantage.

**Best move:** Kxb7

**Main line:** Kxb7 Bxa7 Kxa7

**Motif:** hangingPiece (the knight on b7 is undefended and can be captured)

**Coaching note:**
When your opponent has an undefended piece, capture it! Here, the knight on b7 is under attack by your king and has no defense. After Kxb7, when White recaptures your a7 pawn with Bxa7, your king simply takes the bishop. You win a whole knight and bishop for just a pawn—a decisive material gain. Always look for undefended pieces as your first candidate move.
